title: CinC 2017 reference labels with simulated model scores
citation: Clifford et al. AF classification from a short single lead ECG recording. Computing in Cardiology 2017. doi:10.22489/CinC.2017.065-469
prediction_status: All scores are simulated conditional on recording reference labels. No ECG models were trained or run.

simulation.evidence: One unit-variance Gaussian evidence value per model and recording; its mean is a component drawn from the recording's reference-label mixture.
simulation.shared_noise: Each model's noise is loading * shared + sqrt(1 - loading^2) * own, both standard normal, so the two models' noise terms have correlation loading^2.

models.random_forest: Posterior AF probability under its simulated mixture: a 10% component of AF recordings draws normal-looking evidence and a 16% component shares an ambiguous group with O recordings near probability 0.2. These are mixture weights, not miss rates at any cutoff. Not empirical random-forest performance.
models.resnet: Raw simulated waveform-model score. AF evidence is centred at 3.2, and a 40% mixture component of O recordings draws AF-like evidence centred at 3.0. These are mixture weights, not rates at any cutoff. Deliberately too high and too extreme (overconfident).
models.resnet_calibrated: Platt recalibration of the raw resnet score, fitted on calibration records only; same ranking as resnet.

six_recordings_rule: Development recordings; for each of AF with a high, middle and low forest score and non-AF (O, N, N) with the same bands (above 0.5, 0.26 to 0.5, below 0.2), the recording whose forest score is nearest 0.85, 0.35 and 0.05 (AF) or 0.70, 0.30 and 0.02 (non-AF).

calibration.method: Platt scaling: sigmoid(intercept + slope * logit(resnet)), scikit-learn LogisticRegression(C=inf, solver='newton-cholesky')

limitations: Scores are simulated from reference labels; they are not outputs of trained classifiers.
Recording-level labels only: no interval (window) truth and no patient outcomes.
Noise-labelled recordings retained in the source file, excluded from binary AF analysis.
N and O are AF-negative reference categories, not interchangeable clinical states.
Reference class proportions are not deployment prevalence.
Splits serve a simulated teaching exercise, not patient-level clinical validation.
